body:
From the source (neurosnap/zmx, Zig, docs at zmx.sh) plus probes. Ordered by how much it changes the design.

1. ZMX_DIR isolates everything: a separate socket directory, a separate log directory, a separate world. Verified — a session created under ZMX_DIR=/tmp/zdir1 is invisible to the default namespace and vice versa. Cost: one env var. This is namespacing without a server, per project, per agent, per experiment.
2. Name prefixes are an addressing scheme: `zmx kill 'ns*'` and `zmx wait 's*'` match by prefix (verified). A group of sessions is a name prefix you can act on wholesale.
3. ZMX_SESSION_PREFIX prefixes every name for every command. Verified: name s1 became pres1. It makes names context-dependent, so scripts must carry the prefix; zp documents clearing it before attach for exactly that reason.
4. ZMX_SESSION is set inside the session (verified). `.` names the current session in print-env and history.
5. zmx print sends raw bytes to attached clients' stdout, not through the PTY (verified: the attached client printed it; a detached session showed it on the next attach, because it enters the VT state). Out-of-band display push.
6. Multi-client with a leader policy: last client to send non-escape input bytes becomes leader and owns resize; others are read-only until they type. Verified clients=2 with both receiving output.
7. attach restores the terminal via libghostty-vt (screen, scrollback, mouse modes, kitty keyboard, window title replay). A new client gets the screen, not just future output.
8. OSC 7 cwd tracking (verified by injecting the sequence: cwd changed to file://jail/var). bash does not emit it by default; zsh/fish/nu can. So live cwd is available from any shell that reports it.
9. Per-session log files, {log_dir}/{session}.log, timestamps on every event (see e-zmx-logs).
10. zmx history --vt and --html: truthful styled snapshots with a 256-colour palette, no VT dependency for the caller. --screen/--scrollback N exist on main but not in 0.8.1 (verified: 'session "--screen" does not exist').
11. zmx write types a base64 pipeline into the session's shell (verified in history): `printf '%s' 'BASE64' | base64 -d > 'path'`. Queued behind running work, path relative to the shell at execution, visible in scrollback. A convenience, not a syscall.
12. zmx send is raw bytes to the PTY and accepts stdin (verified driving cat); zmx run is synchronous by default and appends ZMX_TASK_COMPLETED:<4hex>:$?; -d detaches; --fish exists for fish.
13. zmx wait replays already-recorded task outcomes instantly (verified) and prints [epoch] completed task=N exit_code=C; on failure it tails the last 20 lines of the task.
14. ZMX_DIR_MODE / ZMX_LOG_MODE (default 0750/0640) let a group share a socket dir, so group members can attach to and label each other's sessions. Multi-user by permission bit, no auth.
15. zmx is a Zig package too (zmx.run/list/history/kill/create), so the CLI is not the only API — but not from Rust.
title: The affordance inventory: what zmx can already do
